provenance.citation: Shafer, G. (1976). A Mathematical Theory of Evidence. Princeton University Press.
provenance.locus: Chapter 1 / Chapter 4 — the two-witness combination example: two independent witnesses each of reliability 0.9 supporting the same proposition.
provenance.notes: m1(life)=0.9 with 0.1 explicitly on the frame {life,death}; same for witness2. No conflict (K=0). Combined m(life) = 1 - 0.1*0.1 = 0.99 exactly; Bel(life)=0.99. Tolerance 1e-6 (not 1e-9) because BPA masses enter through f32 rule certainties and 0.9 is not exactly representable in binary floating point.
